AMI metadata analysis

Duration is decoded audio frames divided by sample rate. Word density is reference tokens per second, including pauses. Meeting labels come from clip IDs and are checked against an independent evaluation-session catalog.

No ASR or text encoder runs. Group results describe these supplied clips; no confidence intervals or full-dataset estimates are implied.

Audio durations were measured during this evaluation.

12/12 clips reviewed: 10 matching references, 2 mismatches, 0 pending. These human review records cover only the selected cases, not corpus-wide reference accuracy.

Listen and compare with the original reference. Edit metadata_analysis.review.json: set reference_matches_audio to true or false, optionally add corrected_reference and notes, then rerun the same command. Existing answers are preserved.

Interpretation and limits

Word density includes pauses and depends on tokenization, fillers, number rewriting and contraction expansion. It is not pure speaking speed. Word density and WER share reference-word counts, so their association can partly reflect their formulas. Meetings can differ in speakers, content and recording conditions; a difference in WER does not identify a cause. Small groups require caution.

Duration differences, unknown meetings and saved-metadata mismatch details are retained in the companion JSON; no flagged clips are silently removed. This report checks consistency and sensitivity, not independent acoustic truth.

Sources: Pinned CSTR evaluation-session list; Official AMI ASR split; Pinned evaluation data.
